title: How orchestration runs parallel agents safely

subject.lede: Think of a building site with several crews. Before anyone starts, the site manager checks the work orders: no two crews get the same wall at the same time, foundations go in before walls, and every item in the client's brief has a crew. When a crew says "finished", the inspector does not read their note: he walks the site to see which walls really changed, and re-runs the tests the work order named. In 100x the work orders are a task graph (the plan file), the manager is plan_dag, the crews are specialist agents each in their own worktree, and the inspector is agent_report plus the independent verifier. One level down from the 100x-plugin overview page.

tldr.what: Lets several specialist agents build one feature at the same time without editing the same files, and merges nobody's work on their word.
tldr.how: A checker refuses a bad plan before any agent starts; then each agent's report is compared with what git says changed, and its checks are re-run from the plan.
tldr.watch_out: Replay proves a command gave the claimed result, not that the command tests anything, so the plan's verify list must be reviewed before dispatch.

context.purpose: When one feature needs several specialist agents at once (backend, frontend, tests), this is how the main session splits the work so they never edit the same file, and how it checks each agent's "done" before merging instead of taking its word.
context.why_now: Parallel agents fail in three predictable ways: two edit the same shared file, a consumer starts before the contract it builds on exists, and a "tests pass" is merged on trust. Each is visible before or after an agent runs, so each gets a mechanical check.

terms.means: The Claude session you talk to. Only it plans, dispatches agents and merges their work; agents never orchestrate.
The plan file: each task's id, its owner agent, the files it may edit, what it depends on, the acceptance criteria it delivers and the commands that prove it.
terms.example: T1 is the backend engineer's, owns the tagging services folder, and depends on T0.

terms.means: The file patterns a task may edit. Two tasks that can run at the same time must own different files.
A task that owns what others build on: shared types, an API or database schema. Its consumers depend on it and never edit its files.
One observable outcome the spec defines, numbered AC-something. Every one must be owned by a task, and a task may claim only ones the spec defines.
terms.example: The photo page lists its tags, written as one AC line in the spec's acceptance section.

terms.means: Writing the approved spec's path, a hash of its exact bytes and the current commit into the plan. If the spec is edited later, lint fails until someone re-plans.
A group of tasks whose dependencies are all finished, so they run at the same time.
A second checkout of the repository in its own folder. Each running task gets one, so agents never share a working copy.
The JSON block an agent's final message ends with: status, what it understood, what it changed, the commands it ran with their exit codes, and its questions.
A mechanical check that refuses a bad file with numbered errors: here, of the plan before work starts, and of each report after.
Re-running the verify commands the plan declared for a task, and comparing their exit codes with the ones the report claimed.
A read-only agent that re-runs every check itself, tries to make one new test fail, and reports what it finds without fixing anything.

outline.title: plan_dag lint(plan, spec): the plan gate, as pseudocode

lines.code: for t in tasks: reject unknown fields, an unknown owner, empty files / verify / acceptance
for c in t.verify: reject shell syntax outside sh -c, and any commit, push, tag or publish
if find_cycle(by_id): error dependency cycle
for a, b in every pair of tasks:
if a in anc[b] or b in anc[a]: continue   # ordered pairs may share
if any owned glob overlaps: error 'can run in parallel but both own files'
for each consumer of a contract: must depend on it, must not own its files
every AC the spec defines has a task; no task claims an undefined AC
spec_gate: audit passes, status ready, sha256(spec) == stamped spec_sha256
return 1 if errors else 0

outline.title: agent_report lint --graph --cwd: the report gate, as pseudocode

lines.code: base = --base or plan.base or fork_point(worktree) or HEAD
actual = git diff --name-only base  +  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard
if report.agent != task.owner: error
for p in actual: if not path_owned(p, task.files): error 'the worktree changed p, outside'
for p in report.changes: if p not in actual: error 'claimed but no change'
if status == done: every declared verify command is in evidence with exit 0
declared = {argv(v): v for v in task.verify}
for e in report.evidence:
if argv(e.cmd) not in declared: list 'not replayed (undeclared)'
else: run the plan's command as argv, no shell, its own process group
if actual exit != e.exit_code: MISMATCH, print both output tails
return 1 on a mismatch or a missing command; 3 if anything was not replayed

diagrams.title: What orchestration is made of
diagrams.source:
mindmap
  %% level: 2
  root((orchestration))
    The plan
      tasks and owners
      owned files
      contract tasks
    Before agents start
      stamp to the spec
      lint the plan
      waves
    While they run
      one worktree each

    After each report
      lint against git
      replay the declared checks

diagrams.caption: Read outward from the centre: what the plan holds, what is checked before any agent starts, how agents run, and what is checked after each one reports.

diagrams.title: One task, from plan to merge
diagrams.source:
sequenceDiagram
  %% level: 2
  participant Main as Main session
  participant PD as plan_dag
  participant Agent as Specialist agent
  participant WT as Task worktree
  participant AR as agent_report
  Main->>PD: stamp, lint, waves
  PD-->>Main: clean plan and its waves
  Main->>Agent: dispatch prompt with owned files and verify commands
  Agent->>WT: edit owned files, run verify commands
  Agent-->>Main: report as the last json block
  Main->>AR: lint --graph --cwd
  AR->>WT: which files changed since the base?
  alt a file outside the owned files, or a claimed change that is missing
    AR-->>Main: numbered errors, the task goes back
  else clean
    AR-->>Main: no errors
    Main->>AR: replay --yes
    AR->>WT: run the plan's verify commands
    AR-->>Main: reproduced, or MISMATCH
  end
  Main->>PD: next --done
diagrams.caption: Top to bottom: the plan is checked once, then every report is checked twice, first against git and then by re-running the plan's own commands.

diagrams.title: What catches each failure, and when
diagrams.source:
flowchart LR
  %% level: 2
  A[Two parallel tasks own the same file] --> P{plan lint, before any agent starts}
  B[A consumer starts before its contract] --> P
  C[A criterion nobody owns] --> P
  D[An agent edits outside its owned files] --> L{report lint, reads git}
  E[A report claims a file it never changed] --> L
  F[A report claims a check passed] --> R{replay of the plan's commands}
  P --> X[plan refused: fix the plan]
  L --> Y[report refused: the task goes back]
  R --> Y
diagrams.caption: Left, the failure; middle, the check that finds it. Plan problems are caught before anyone works; report problems are caught before anything merges.

diagrams.title: A task's states, as plan next sees them
diagrams.source:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> waiting
  waiting --> ready: every dependency done
  waiting --> held: a dependency is blocked
  held --> ready: the blocker is answered
  ready --> running: dispatched with its wave
  running --> done: report lints and replays
  running --> ready: report rejected
  running --> blocked: needs-decision
  blocked --> ready: question answered
  done --> [*]
diagrams.caption: A blocked task pauses only the tasks that depend on it; everything else keeps running.

scenarios.title: One feature, three waves: plan, run in parallel, check, merge

steps.t: The main session stamps the plan against the approved spec
steps.d: Stamp refuses a spec that has not passed its audit, then writes the spec's path, a hash of its exact bytes and the current commit into the plan.
code: refuse unless audit_spec(spec) is clean and ready

steps.t: Lint checks the whole plan before any agent starts
steps.d: It re-hashes the spec (an edit since the stamp fails), looks for dependency cycles, checks that tasks able to run at the same time own different files, and that every acceptance criterion has an owner.

steps.t: Waves: the plan splits into groups that can run together
steps.d: A wave is every task whose dependencies are all finished. Here the contract task T0 runs alone, then T1 and T2 together, then the end-to-end tests in T3.
do: {{waves_n}} waves; the widest runs {{widest}} at once

steps.t: Wave one: the contract task runs alone and merges
steps.d: The shared types and API shape land first, so neither consumer builds against a contract that does not exist yet. Its report passes the same two checks shown later for T1.

steps.t: Plan next: T1 and T2 are ready now
Both wave-two tasks are dispatched in one message, each with its own worktree
steps.d: Each agent gets the dispatch prompt: its goal, its worktree, the files it may edit, the criteria it delivers and the verify commands it must run.
code: dispatch T1 and T2 in one message

steps.t: Each agent edits only its owned files, then runs its verify commands
steps.d: The protocol every specialist follows: understand, list gaps, challenge the plan, stop if blocked, do the thinnest slice, verify, report.

steps.t: Each agent ends with its report as the last JSON block
steps.d: Earlier JSON blocks in the message are treated as drafts or examples; only the last one is the report.

steps.t: Report lint asks git which files changed, not the report
steps.d: Committed, staged, unstaged and new files all count, measured from the commit the plan was stamped at. Each must sit inside the task's owned files, and each file the report claims must really have changed.

steps.t: Replay re-runs only the verify commands the plan declared
steps.d: Each runs as a plain argument list with no shell, in its own process group, with a time limit of {{timeout_s}}. A command only the report mentions is never run.

steps.t: The independent verifier repeats the checks and tries to break one test
steps.d: It trusts no report: it re-runs the declared commands itself, breaks the behaviour one new test covers to prove that test can fail, and never repairs what it finds.
do: reproduced; the broken test failed as it should

steps.t: Merge the wave, verify the whole, and T3 becomes ready
steps.d: Only the main session merges. The project's full checks run on the merged result before the next wave starts.

scenarios.title: What if two parallel tasks owned the same file?

steps.t: The plan gives T1 and T2 the same module file, with no order between them
steps.d: T1 owns every module file in the tagging folder; T2 also lists the one module file it wants to register its page in.
do: T1 and T2 both own the module file

steps.t: Nothing checks the plan, so both are dispatched at once
Both agents edit the same module file, each in its own worktree
steps.d: Separate worktrees hide the clash while they work; it surfaces only when the branches meet.

steps.t: At merge the two edits conflict, or one silently replaces the other

scenarios.title: Fix: plan lint refuses the overlap before any agent starts

steps.t: Lint refuses the plan: T1 and T2 can run in parallel but both own files
steps.d: Pairs with a dependency path between them are skipped; every other pair has its file patterns compared. The comparison can over-report, never under-report.
do: error: T1 and T2 both own the module file

steps.t: The fix goes in the plan: one task depends on the other, or the shared file moves to a contract task
do: module file owned by T1 only

plan.tasks: module file owned by T1 only

steps.t: Lint is clean again, and only then do agents start

scenarios.title: What if a report were merged on its word?

steps.t: T3's agent writes no test file, and edits T1's service file instead
steps.d: T3 owns only the end-to-end test file. Its edit is outside that, and nothing in the report will mention it.
do: service file edited; no test file

steps.t: Its report claims the test file and says the check passed, all green
Merged on its word: no tests exist, and T1's service changed behind its back
do: untested, and the service was overwritten

scenarios.title: Fix: lint compares the report with git, and replay re-runs the plan's check

steps.t: Lint asks git: the service file changed, outside T3's owned files
steps.d: The report never mentions that file; git does. Whatever the report says, a changed file outside the task's owned files fails it.
do: error: the worktree changed the service file, outside T3's files

vars.changed: service file edited; no test file

steps.t: Lint also finds the claimed test file is not there
do: error: change claimed, but the worktree has none

steps.t: Replay re-runs the declared check: claimed success, actual failure
steps.d: It runs the command the plan declared for T3, not the text in the report, and prints both output tails side by side.
do: MISMATCH: claimed exit zero, actual one

steps.t: Rejected: the task goes back to its agent, and nothing merges
do: rejected: fix it and report again

options.label: Check the plan before work, and each report against git and a replay after
pros: Collisions are refused before any agent spends time
A report's claims are tested, not believed: git for files, the plan for commands
cons: Replay checks exit codes, not that a command means anything: a plan that declares true replays fine
File-overlap checks can over-report; split the patterns

options.label: Merge each agent's report on its word
cons: An edit outside the task's files is never seen

options.label: Run one agent at a time in one checkout
pros: No two agents ever touch the same file at once
cons: Wall time grows with every task
Still merges each report on its word

options.label: Re-run whatever commands the report lists
cons: A report could prove done with a command that always succeeds

decision.deciding_factor: A report is written by the party being judged, so every claim in it is re-derived from the plan, git and a real run.
decision.revisit_when: A task needs proof an exit code cannot give, such as a screenshot or a live response, and that proof becomes common.

checks.q: The report lists the files it changed. Which list does lint trust?
checks.answer: Git's: it asks git what changed in the worktree since the stamped commit, and compares that with the task's owned files and with the report's list.

checks.q: T1 and T2 both list the module file. When is that caught?
checks.answer: Before any agent starts: plan lint refuses the plan, so nobody does work that would collide.

checks.q: The report says the check passed. Does replay run the command the report wrote?
checks.answer: No: it runs the command the plan declared for that task and compares exit codes; evidence for any other command is listed as not replayed.

notes.load_plan: Reads the plan file; prints why and returns nothing when it is missing, not JSON, or has no task list.
notes.find_cycle: Depth-first walk over the dependency edges; returns the first cycle as a list of task ids, or nothing.
notes.lint: The plan gate: field shapes, owners, verify commands, cycles, file overlap between unordered tasks, contract rules and acceptance coverage against the spec.
notes.file_sha256: The sha256 of a file's exact bytes: what stamp records and lint compares.
notes.cmd_lint: The lint command: finds the stamped spec (or the one given), runs lint and the spec gate, prints numbered errors, fails on any.
notes.cmd_stamp: The stamp command: refuses a spec that fails its audit or is not ready, then writes the spec path, its hash and the current commit into the plan.
notes.cmd_waves: The waves command: prints each wave's tasks, owners and titles, and how many run at once in the widest wave.
notes.cmd_next: The next command: given finished and blocked tasks, lists what is ready now, what is held behind a blocked task, and what is still waiting.

notes._plan_checks: The plan-aware rows: every claimed and every real changed file inside the owned files, every claimed change present, every declared verify command in the evidence.
notes.cmd_extract: The extract command: saves the message's last JSON block as the report file, refusing a write a planted symlink would redirect.
notes.cmd_lint: The lint command: with a plan it requires the worktree, resolves the base, asks git for the real changes, then prints notes, warnings and numbered errors.
notes.cmd_replay: The replay command: sorts evidence into declared, undeclared and refused, runs only the declared commands after a yes, and prints each mismatch with both output tails.
notes.cmd_summary: The summary command: merges questions (deduplicated), plan issues and findings across reports, blocking first, capped at one batch.
